effect_scopes.analysis_strategy: Modified assignment analysis: 175 participants were randomized, then 6 participants (3 per group) were excluded from all analyses after reintervention; the Report states there was no crossover or study-drug administration error.

source_spans.exact_text: In the period December 2016 to March 2019, 175 patients were randomly assigned to the present study ( Fig 2 ). Six patients (3 in each group) were excluded from the analyses because they underwent reintervention (had a prespecified exclusion criteria). No crossover and no mistake in the study drug administration occurred.

effect_scopes.analysis_strategy: Reported analysis uses the randomized groups of 32 participants each; the delirium result is reported for those same two allocated groups (3.1% versus 15.6%).

source_spans.exact_text: Sixty-four patients scheduled for elective cardiac surgery consented to participate in the study. After surgery, patients were transferred intubated and ventilated to a cardiothoracic intensive care unit (ICU) and then were prospectively randomized in a double-blind fashion into one of the two groups using computer. Group A ( n = 32) received a 12 h infusion of normal saline and Group B ( n = 32) received a 12 h infusion of dexmedetomidine 0.4 μg/kg/h without a loading dose.
A reduced trend in delirium incidence was noted in dexmedetomidine group (3.1%) than in saline group (15.6%) with P = 0.086+ [ Table 4 ].
